title_en: Dipan Patel on Permira’s ‘Artisanal’ Approach to Private Equity
title_zh: Dipan Patel 谈 Permira 的「匠人式」私募股权之道
subtitle_zh: Permira 联席 CEO 分享匠人式投资哲学、AI 颠覆判断及反脆弱组织文化
summary_zh: 本期 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 的 Great Investors 系列由 Allison Moss 对话 Permira 联席管理合伙人兼联席 CEO Dipan Patel。Permira 是横跨私募股权与信贷的全球投资公司，管理资产约 1000 亿美元：1985 年由四人从 Schroders 拿到 4800 万美元起步。私募股权覆盖消费、医疗、服务与科技四大板块，聚焦企业价值（EV）约 2 亿至 20 亿美元的中型市场。Patel 总结了几项独特优势：90 年代末设立首支泛欧洲基金，使美欧投资与人员大致对半；“数字核心、多板块”模式，最佳机会出现在数字与实体经济板块的交叉点；刻意的增长基因——典型标的是低杠杆、低利润率、高增长，靠投入新产品、新渠道、新地区与商业模式转型拉长增长跑道，以便最终说服产业买家；以及始终私人持有的合伙制，把回报绑定在成果与激励对齐上。他提出行业正分化为“工厂模式”与“手工匠人模式”，Permira 属于后者，吸引愿意长时间孵化投资主题、把一笔交易从头做透、接受不频繁出手的人。Patel 的职业起点格外沉重——2002 年在 Arthur Andersen 遇上安然事件，随后在 Lehman Brothers 经历 2008 年金融危机；他从这两家崩塌的企业里提炼出文化崩溃的共同特征：魅力型领导、过度自信、冒险常态化、无人敢对权力讲真话、激励错配，并把“不要变成 Lehman 或 Arthur Andersen”列为首要准则。关于 AI，他的判断是“好事会降临到好公司头上，坏事会发生在坏公司身上”，AI 只是加速这个过程：靠同质化渠道聚合大宗商品数据的企业已在衰退曲线上，拥有专有数据、网络效应、强品牌与垂直定制体验的企业则站在正确一侧。他还强调 DPI 应是一种运营节奏而非一次性事件。
description: Dipan Patel on Permira’s ‘Artisanal’ Approach to Private Equity

turns.en: Good things happen to good companies and bad things happen to bad companies. And I think what AI is doing is just accelerating those things.
turns.zh: 好事会降临到好公司头上，坏事会发生在坏公司身上。我觉得 AI 正在做的，就是加速这个过程。

turns.en: So if you're a business that aggregates commodity data, sells it through a commodity channel with a commodity UX, you were probably already on a decline curve.
turns.zh: 所以，如果你的业务只是在聚合大宗商品数据，通过一个同质化的渠道、用一套同质化的用户体验去卖，那你大概率已经在衰退曲线上了。

turns.en: If you're a company with proprietary data and with network effects, an incredibly strong brand, and you've built a user experience which is built for the idiosyncrasies of a vertical, probably you're going to be on the right side of AI.
turns.zh: 如果你的公司拥有专有数据、有网络效应、有极强的品牌，并且你打造的用户体验是专门针对某个垂直行业的独特需求设计的——那你大概率会站在 AI 的正确一侧。

turns.en: Welcome to Goldman Sachs Exchange as great investors. I'm Allison Mass. I'm about to sit down with Dupont Patel, co-managing partner and co-CEO of Primera, a global investment firm spanning private equity and credit with approximately $100 billion in assets under management.
turns.zh: 欢迎来到 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 的 Great Investors 系列。我是 Allison Moss。接下来我要和 Dipan Patel 坐下来聊聊，他是 Permira 的联席管理合伙人兼联席 CEO。Permira 是一家横跨私募股权和信贷的全球投资公司，管理资产规模约 1000 亿美元。

turns.en: So welcome to great investors. So great to have you here. Thank you for having me. So everyone remembers their first job, but yours must have been especially memorable.
turns.zh: 欢迎参加 Great Investors。很高兴你来到这里。谢谢们邀请我。每个人都记得自己的第一份工作，但你的第一份工作一定格外令人难忘。

turns.en: You worked at Arthur Anderson in 2002, and then after university you went to Lehman Brothers. Those must have been fascinating experiences. So tell us a little bit about them.
turns.zh: 你 2002 年在 Arthur Andersen 工作过，大学毕业后又到了 Lehman Brothers。这些经历一定非常精彩，跟我们讲讲吧。

turns.en: Yeah, that's right. I worked at Arthur Anderson in 2002 during the Enron scandal, and then Lehman Brothers in 2008, obviously during the global financial crisis.
turns.zh: 没错。我 2002 年在 Arthur Andersen 工作，正好赶上安然事件；然后是 Lehman Brothers，2008 年，显然就是全球金融危机期间。

turns.en: Formative, to see two iconic companies struggle and then eventually fall before us 30 was something that once you see it, it's hard to unsee it and leaves lasting memories and a lot of learnings.
turns.zh: 那是塑造性的经历——亲眼看着两家标志性企业在自己面前挣扎、然后倒下，这种场景一旦看过就很难忘记，留下了持久的记忆和大量的教训。

turns.en: Yeah. So tell us about Primera today. For those who aren't familiar, what makes Primera unique and maybe tie in some of the lessons that you learned from earlier in your career that have helped you lead Primera today?
turns.zh: 好的。跟我们说说今天的 Permira 吧。对于不太了解的人来说，Permira 有什么独特之处？也许可以结合你早期职业生涯中学到的一些经验，讲讲它们如何帮助你今天领导 Permira。

turns.en: So Primera started in 1985 as four people, $48 million from Schrader's Bank. Over the last 41 years, if you wind the clock forward, the business has raised more than $100 billion a capital.
turns.zh: Permira 1985 年创立时只有四个人，从 Schroders 银行拿了 4800 万美元起步。过去 41 年，把时钟往前拨，这家机构累计募集了超过 1000 亿美元的资本。

turns.en: We have about 500 people, 250 investors, 16 offices globally. We invest in private equity and in credit. Our private equity business invests really across four sectors, consumer, health care services and technology.
turns.zh: 我们有大约 500 名员工、250 位投资人士、全球 16 个办公室。我们投私募股权和信贷。我们的私募股权业务覆盖四个板块：消费、医疗、服务和科技。

turns.en: It does it primarily across the mid-market to think businesses in the kind of 200 million EV, up to 2 billion EV range. And everything we do is really significant minorities, a governance with teeth all the way through to full control and to very active owners.
turns.zh: 主要聚焦中型市场，企业 EV（企业价值）大概在 2 亿到 20 亿美元的区间。我们做的一切从有实质权力的少数股权、到完全控股、再到非常积极的股东参与，都涵盖在内。

turns.en: Then our credit business invests across private credit through to liquid credit and right through the risk return spectrum. You ask the question around what makes us unique and what was our edge.
turns.zh: 然后我们的信贷业务从私募信贷到流动性信贷，贯穿整个风险收益谱系。你问我们独特在哪里、优势在哪里。

turns.en: I say it's a few different things. The first thing is, Primera raised the first pan-European fund in the late 90s. And as a result, we built Boots on the Ground right across Europe and just dense networks, relationships, footprints.
turns.zh: 我觉得有几个方面。第一，Permira 在 90 年代末设立了第一支泛欧洲基金。因此我们在整个欧洲都扎下了根，有非常密集的网络、关系和布局。

turns.en: And that served us really well. That's 50% of our investing today. At the same time, we're probably one of the very few firms that have an equal weighted US and European business.
turns.zh: 这一点让我们受益匪深，那是我们今天 50% 投资的来源。同时我们可能是极少数美国和欧洲业务完全对半开的公司之一。

turns.en: About 50% of our people sit in US, 50% are in Europe. 50% of our capital deployed and capital returned have come from both regions. So that's one.
turns.zh: 大约 50% 的人在美国，50% 在欧洲。我们投入和回收的资本大约一半来自每个地区。这是第一点。

turns.en: We have what we call digital core multi-sector. So we're very deep in digital. But the most interesting aspect of our investing has always been at the intersection of digital and our real economy sectors, so consumer health care and services.
turns.zh: 我们有所谓的“数字核心、多板块”模式。我们在数字化方面非常深入。但我们投资最有意思的部分一直是在数字与实体经济板块的交叉点上——也就是消费、医疗和服务。

turns.en: And that's where we have a particular edge, like a real economy business where there is a significant value question underwrite in the realm of digital is Power Alley for Primera.
turns.zh: 那正是我们拥有独特优势的地方。比如一个实体经济企业，如果存在通过数字化手段来显著提升价值、重新定义估值逻辑的机会，那就是 Permira 的主场。

turns.en: We have a very strong growth DNA. So we've probably got one of the fastest growing portfolios in the larger cap end of P. Our portfolio consistently grows organically low teens, top line and significantly higher at the bottom line.
turns.zh: 我们有很强的增长基因。在大型私募股权基金中，我们大概拥有增长最快的投资组合之一。我们的组合持续保持低双位数的有机收入增长，而利润端增速还要高得多。

turns.en: That's by design. We over-index to growth year businesses. The typical Primera business will be under-levered, under-margined and over-growthed.
turns.zh: 这是有意设计的。我们超配增长型企业。一家典型的 Permira 企业的画像是：低杠杆、低利润率、高增长。

turns.en: And we really like that formula. In the end, when you're selling businesses, particularly selling businesses to strategics, you are trying to convince someone that there is a long growth runway.
turns.zh: 我们非常喜欢这个公式。最终，当你出售企业时——尤其是卖给产业买家——你实际上是在说服对方：这里有很长的增长跑道。

turns.en: And you don't get there by under-investing in a business and milking a business over your investment period. So we tend to invest really deeply in new products, new channels, new geographies.
turns.zh: 而你不能靠投资期内对企业投入不足、挤奶式经营来做到这一点。所以我们会非常深入地投入新产品、新渠道、新地区。

turns.en: We often do business model transitions. But growth underwrites are central to anything that comes through our investment committee. And then the last thing is we are a private company.
turns.zh: 我们经常做商业模式的转型。但增长假设是我们投委会讨论的核心。最后一点是，我们是一家私人持有的公司。

turns.en: It's not unique. There are a bunch of scale private equity funds. It's increasingly becoming important. Over time, we're a private partnership.
turns.zh: 这并不独特，有很多大型私募股权基金都是私人持有的。但这一点正变得越来越重要。从创立至今，我们一直是一个私人合伙制机构。

turns.en: Since inception, that's not changed. We're owned by our partners. And that goes ultimately to outcomes and performance and incentives and alignment.
turns.zh: 从成立到现在这一点从未改变。我们的合伙人拥有这家公司。归根到底，这关系到成果、业绩、激励和对齐。

turns.en: In what ways does being private and remaining private help with your investment culture and with retaining talent and recruiting talent? So Primera is built by investors for investors.
turns.zh: 私人持有、始终保持私有化，对投资文化以及留住和招募人才有什么帮助？Permira 是由投资人打造的、为投资人服务的公司。

turns.en: And so we want and attract people who are craftspeople, right? So I think the industry is bifurcating between more like factory models and artisanal models.
turns.zh: 所以我们吸引和需要的是匠人型人才。我觉得整个行业正在分化为两种模式：工厂模式和手工匠人模式。

turns.en: Right, and you're an artisanal model. Yeah, you know, there's no right or wrong in these models. And both these models will work, but they are definitely different and they attract different types of people.
turns.zh: 对，你们走的是匠人模式。嗯，你知道，这两种模式没有对错之分。它们都能成功，但确实非常不同，吸引的人也不同。

turns.en: And if you're someone who likes to craft an investment thesis, think differently, work a deal, is comfortable with really long gestation periods, wants to be an absolute expert in their space, is frankly comfortable not doing deals and not being in the cadence of just allocating assets.
turns.zh: 如果你喜欢精心打磨一个投资主题、用不同的方式思考、把一笔交易从头到尾做透，能接受很长的孵化周期，希望在自己领域成为绝对的专家，坦率地说可以接受不频繁出手、不处在那种不断配置资产的节奏里——

turns.en: Primera is going to be the place for you. And if you want to build new products and new channels and new business lines, there'll be other firms that are, you know, better homes for those people.
turns.zh: Permira 就是最适合你的地方。如果你想不断搭建新产品、新渠道、新业务线，那会有其他机构更适合那些人。

turns.en: But Primera is the craftsman's place of work. Yeah, that's a great way to describe it. So thank you for that. So you've been at Primera since 2009.
turns.zh: 但 Permira 是匠人的工坊。嗯，这个形容太好了。谢谢你这么说。你在 Permira 从 2009 年一直到现在。

turns.en: Was there any particular deal from early in your career that you're especially proud of? We did a deal taking a company called Renaissance Learning Private in the US.
turns.zh: 早期职业生涯里有没有哪笔交易让你特别自豪？我们做过一笔交易，把美国一家叫 Renaissance Learning 的公司私有化了。

turns.en: It was an ed tech company. It was sold into 70,000 schools and ended up selling it in two and a half years. We made more than four times the money, did a range of things with that company, and I was fortunate to be involved in it.
turns.zh: 它是一家教育科技公司，产品卖进了 7 万所学校。我们持有两年半就把它卖掉了，回报超过 4 倍。期间我们做了一系列事情，我很幸运参与其中。

turns.en: The reason why it's special for me was, and I think it actually says a lot about our firm. When I joined, and I think we do this a lot with our junior talent, we really encourage thematic, thesis driven work from right at the beginning of people's career journeys and in the firm.
turns.zh: 这笔交易对我特殊的原因——我觉得它实际上也说明了这家公司的文化。我加入的时候，我想我们对年轻人才一直也是这样做的——我们非常鼓励从职业生涯一开始就做主题性的、假设驱动的研究。

turns.en: And I went off and I started working on a thematic piece in ed tech. I remember coming up with something called the Global Top 10. I know this company is that I thought would be interesting to me.
turns.zh: 然后我就去做了一份教育科技领域的主题研究报告。我记得当时列了一个“全球 Top 10”清单，把我觉得有意思的公司排进去。

turns.en: And Renaissance on that top 10. Renaissance Learning was on that top 10. And I was relatively new to the industry and I went to my principal at that time.
turns.zh: Renaissance Learning 就在那个 Top 10 名单里。当时我入行时间还不长，我就去找我那时候的上司——也就是 principal（项目负责人）。

turns.en: He's now actually as a partner in the firm and said, look, I've been doing this work and what do you think? And actually funny thing, I'd reached out to a guy called Barry O'Brien, who was I think then probably a VP at Goldman Sachs.
turns.zh: 他现在已经是公司的合伙人了——我说：我做了这个研究，你怎么看？有意思的是，我当时联系了一个叫 Barry O’Brien 的人，他那时候大概是 Goldman Sachs 的 VP。

turns.en: Yes, who now runs our TMT business globally. And he put me in touch with Terry and Judy Paul who owned the company. And I said to the guys there, should I just go?
turns.zh: 对，他现在负责我们在全球的 TMT 业务。他帮我和公司的创始人 Terry 和 Judy Paul 搭上了线。然后我就跟我们的同事说，我要不要去见一见？

turns.en: And they said, sure, just go. And I was an associate in the firm. They said, just call this guy on the West Coast because it's a US thing. And so I called a guy called Brian Reuder and we went along to the meeting.
turns.zh: 他们说，当然，去就是了。当时我职级还只是 associate（经理）。他们说，你直接联系西海岸的那个人就好，因为这是美国的项目。然后我就打了个电话给 Brian Ruder，我们一起去见了面。

turns.en: I was in Denver and one thing led to another. And we ended up prosecuting that deal and taking that company private. And the great thing about it for me was, and I think about it a lot with the junior talent we have in the organization, is that idea came from a junior person.
turns.zh: 我在 Denver，然后一件接一件，最后我们就推进了那笔交易，把公司私有化了。对我来说最棒的一点——我经常跟组织里的年轻人聊这件事——那个想法来自一个初级人员。

turns.en: It also came because that junior person was encouraged to go take that thread as far as they possibly could. It was fascinating for me because the things we did with that business, we shut down a hardware division.
turns.zh: 同时，这也是因为那个初级人员被鼓励沿着那条线索尽可能往前推。对我很有启发，因为我们在那家企业做的事情包括——关掉了硬件部门。

turns.en: We transitioned the whole business model to SaaS. We entered a new country. We invested in this whole new math product. We did that all in the course of about three years and got rewarded for all of it.
turns.zh: 把整个商业模式转成了 SaaS，进入了一个新国家，投资了一整套全新的数学产品。我们在大约三年内完成了所有这些事情，然后都得到了回报。

turns.en: So it was a vignette of good stuff. I got spoiled because I probably ended that and thought- He said, this is easy. This is how privacy works, right?
turns.zh: 所以那是一个好的缩影。我有点被宠坏了——因为我做完那笔交易之后可能觉得，哦，这挺简单的嘛，私募股权不就是这样吗？

turns.en: And so, yeah, special place in my heart that investment. And thank you to Barry. Yeah, I love the story how it originates with a call to golden sex.
turns.zh: 所以，是的，那笔投资在我心里有特别的位置。也要谢谢 Barry。嗯，我喜欢这个故事——因为它从打电话给 Goldman Sachs 开始。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, I'll tell Barry that. And Brian, the first deal with Brian. So now you share the top job for that premiere with Brian. How did that come about?
turns.zh: 好的，我会把这话转告给 Barry。还有 Brian——你和 Brian 的第一笔交易。现在你和 Brian 共同执掌 Permira 的最高位置，这是怎么实现的？

turns.en: And how do you split up responsibilities or look at being co-managing partners? Yeah, so Brian and I have worked together for a long time. So actually, after we did Renaissance Learning together, Brian called me at some point and said, take a look at this business called ancestry.com.
turns.zh: 你们怎么分工，或者说怎么看待联席管理合伙人这个模式？嗯，Brian 和我合作很久了。实际上，做完 Renaissance Learning 之后，有一天 Brian 打电话给我说，你看一下这个叫 ancestry.com 的业务。

turns.en: And long story short, we took that company private and made nearly four times the money on that investment. And in the middle of that, he said, why don't you come out to the West Coast?
turns.zh: 长话短说，我们把那家公司私有化了，获得了将近 4 倍的回报。在那笔交易中间，他说你为什么不搬到西海岸来？

turns.en: So I moved out to the West Coast and I worked in- What year was that? That was in 2012. Okay. And I was in our Menlo Park office, which is now 40 people.
turns.zh: 于是我就搬到了西海岸，在——那是哪一年？2012 年。好的。我在我们的 Menlo Park 办公室，现在那里有 40 个人了。

turns.en: And by the time it was four or five of us. And so I got to know Brian there and we worked together on lots of lots of deals. Ancestry and then many other deals had together after that.
turns.zh: 当时只有四五个人的规模。然后我在那里跟 Brian 更熟了，一起做了很多很多交易。Ancestry，然后之后还有很多我们一起做的交易。

turns.en: So we had a long, very long working relationship. Amir has done five leadership transitions in its 41 year history. The common themes have always been the two co-managing partners or the new co-managing partners has been in internal promote.
turns.zh: 所以我们有非常非常长的合作关系。Permira 在 41 年的历史里经历了五次领导层交接。共同主题一直是——新的联席管理合伙人都是内部晋升。

turns.en: And the existing leadership or leader has stayed in the organization for a handful of years and been very active. So that's been very consistent in terms of the way that this leadership transition has worked.
turns.zh: 现有的领导或领导者会在组织中继续待上好几年，并且非常活跃。所以这个领导层过渡的方式一直非常一致。

turns.en: Brian and I, as I said, we've worked together for a long time. I was based in the US, I'm best in Europe. We both grew up in tech, but he co-round tech.
turns.zh: Brian 和我，如我所说，合作很久了。他常驻美国，我常驻欧洲。我们都是从科技板块成长起来的，他后来联席负责科技。

turns.en: I went on to co-run the consumer teams, that's two of our biggest sectors. And we tend to have a co-leadership model. We like that model, I think Goldman Sachs has a fair amount of co-leadership in your sectors and geographies too.
turns.zh: 我后来联席负责消费板块——那是我们最大的两个板块之一。我们倾向于用联席领导的模式。我们喜欢这个模式，我想 Goldman Sachs 在你们的板块和地区里也有很多联席领导。

turns.en: It was a natural evolution a couple of years ago when Kurt moved up to Executive Chairman and Tom had left the business. I would say the most important thing and of course Brian and I, we have our splits and obviously across geography and sectors and things like that.
turns.zh: 几年前，当 Kurt 升任 Executive Chairman、Tom 离开公司之后，这自然就成了下一步。我想说的是，当然 Brian 和我之间有分工——在地区和板块上之类的。

turns.en: The most important thing is we make eight to ten really important investing decisions every year. We make about eight to ten really important exit decisions every year.
turns.zh: 但最重要的事情是，我们每年做 8 到 10 个真正重要的投资决策，每年做大约 8 到 10 个真正重要的退出决策。

turns.en: And less important is how we split the this and the that of the organization and more important is how we come together and the investment committee comes together to make just as many world class decisions as we possibly can.
turns.zh: 不太重要的是怎么划分组织的这块那块，更重要的是我们如何走到一起、投委会如何走到一起，尽可能做出更多世界级的决策。

turns.en: As I said earlier, we're a private company and most of our economics are tied up in the outcomes that we drive and those decisions are the most important things we do every single year.
turns.zh: 如我前面所说，我们是一家私人公司，我们大部分的经济回报都绑定在我们驱动的结果上。那些决策才是我们每年做的事情中最关键的。

turns.en: And if we get them right, we can get a lot of other things wrong. And if we get them wrong, there's any number of things we can get right and it won't make up for it.
turns.zh: 如果这些决策做对了，其他很多事情做偏了也没关系。但如果这些决策做错了，其他再多事情做对了都弥补不了。

turns.en: Sounds like a great partnership and a long-standing partnership. So as you mentioned, Premiere has built dedicated sector teams in tech and consumer services and healthcare long before that was standard practice and private equity.
turns.zh: 听起来是一段很棒的、很长久的合作关系。正如你提到的，Permira 很早就建立了专门的板块团队——科技、消费、服务和医疗——远早于这在私募股权成为标准做法。

turns.en: So how does AI affect that calculus? There's a perception that a lot of private equity backed companies stand to be disrupted by AI. So how do you take that into account in your investment committee process?
turns.zh: 那么 AI 如何影响这个判断？有一种看法认为很多私募股权支持的企业会被 AI 颠覆。你们在投委会流程中如何考虑这一点？

turns.en: So good things happen to good companies and bad things happen to bad companies. And we think of good companies as companies with strong modes and bad companies as companies that lack modes and obviously that's a spectrum.
turns.zh: 好公司会有好事发生，坏公司会有坏事发生。我们把好公司定义为拥有强大护城河（moat）的公司，把坏公司定义为缺乏护城河的公司——当然这是一个光谱。

turns.en: I think what AI is doing is just accelerating those things. So if you're a business that aggregates commodity data, sells it through a commodity channel with a commodity UX, you were probably already on a decline curve and AI is going to accelerate that.
turns.zh: 我觉得 AI 正在做的，只是加速这个过程。如果你的业务只是在聚合同质化数据、通过同质化渠道、用同质化 UX 去卖，那你大概率已经在衰退曲线上了，而 AI 会加速这个衰退。

turns.en: And if you're a company with proprietary data and with network effects, an incredibly strong brand and you've built a user experience which is built for the idiosyncrasies of a vertical, probably you're going to be on the right side of AI.
turns.zh: 如果你的公司拥有专有数据、网络效应、极强的品牌，并且你打造的用户体验是专门针对某个垂直行业的独特需求——那你大概率会站在 AI 的正确一侧。

turns.en: And you are probably succeeding anyway. And AI is going to allow you to add an intelligence layer on top of what you already have and then monetize that.
turns.zh: 而且你本来就已经在成功了。AI 会让你能在已有的基础上叠加一个智能层，然后把它变现。

turns.en: The private industry's probably got a mixture of good and bad companies. And I think the metric that we think about in our firm is, how much of our nav is, do we feel happy about when Dario opens his mouth?
turns.zh: 私募行业里面大概好坏公司都有。我觉得我们公司内部思考的一个指标是：当 Dario Amodei 开口说话的时候，我们有多少净值是我们不担心的？

turns.en: Or when Anthropic drops a model? And honestly that number was, we were figuring that out probably two, three years ago and we're probably on the defense.
turns.zh: 或者当 Anthropic 发布一个新模型的时候。老实说，两三年前我们研究这个问题的时候大概处于防守态势。

turns.en: Today we're definitely on the offense on that and that metric is only going up and to the right. But if I look out across the entire private industry, I don't know the stats but the reality is there is a mixture.
turns.zh: 今天我们在这一点上绝对是处于进攻态势，而且这个指标只会继续往右上方走。但如果我看整个私募行业，我不知道具体数据，但现实是好的坏的都有。

turns.en: And for sure 100% of the nav sitting in the private industry is not on the right side of AI and is not benefiting every time a new model is released.
turns.zh: 可以肯定的是，私募行业 100% 的净值并不都在 AI 的正确一侧，并不是每次新模型发布时都能从中受益。

turns.en: So are there specific sectors or sub sectors where you're looking to deploy capital now? Yep, so first of all, just seeming back, it's a fascinating time to be alive.
turns.zh: 那你们现在有没有具体想投入的板块或子板块？嗯，首先，退后一步来看，这是一个活着的奇妙时代。

turns.en: It's also very stressful and sometimes confusing time to be alive. And I always like the McKinsey analogy of you've got the microscope in one hand and you've got the telescope in the other.
turns.zh: 同时也是一个非常紧张、有时令人困惑的时代。我一直很喜欢麦肯键的那个比喻：你一只手里拿着显微镜，另一只手拿着望远镜。

turns.en: When you look down the microscope, the list of problems with the wall of worry is endless, right? You have government indebtedness, you have potential rate hikes, you have more armed conflicts in the world today than any time since Second World War.
turns.zh: 当你用显微镜往下看，那一堵“忧虑之墙”上的问题是无穷无尽的。你有政府债务负担，有潜在加息，今天世界上有比二战以来任何时候都多的武装冲突。

turns.en: You have the threat of unemployment from AI and I could go on and on and on. At the same time, you've got a major platform shift, which is super early innings and is going to reshape industries and reshape profit pools.
turns.zh: 你有 AI 带来的失业威胁——我可以一直说下去。但与此同时，你有一个重大的平台转换，还处于非常早期的阶段，它将重塑行业、重塑利润池。

turns.en: You have energy transition where power demand is going to double over some period of time. And at the same time, half of the grid capacity is going to need to be retired.
turns.zh: 你有能源转型——电力需求在某个时间跨度内要翻倍，同时一半的电网容量需要退役。

turns.en: You have major advances in the medical field. You have a country in India, which is going to come online and try very significant growth over the next 20 years.
turns.zh: 你有医学领域的重大突破。你有印度这个国家即将上线，在未来 20 年试图实现非常显著的增长。

turns.en: So you've got these kind of two things in your hand at the same time. And I think as a leader, you've got to take a distanced view of the stuff that's close up and a close view of the stuff that's far away.
turns.zh: 所以你两只手里同时拿着这些东西。我觉得作为领导者，你必须对近处的东西保持距离感，对远处的东西保持贴近感。

turns.en: And that's what we try and do in the organization and just think really long term. And think about our exit environment and try and skate to where the puck's going rather than where the puck is.
turns.zh: 这就是我们在这家组织里试着做的事情——真正长远地思考。思考退出环境，试着滑向冰球将要去的地方而不是它现在的位置。

turns.en: All of those things and those big, let's call it, telescope things, they'll be expressed through our sectors, I think, in different ways. I think within software, it's going to be about adding an intelligence layer and monetizing that over time.
turns.zh: 所有这些大的——我们叫它望远镜层面的事情——会通过我们的板块以不同方式体现。我觉得在软件领域，关键是要叠加一个智能层，然后随着时间把它变现。

turns.en: I think within services, there will be fascinating things to do in engineering services, in blue collar services, in consumer. I think AI is going to radically transform personalization.
turns.zh: 在服务领域，工程服务、蓝领服务、消费板块都会有非常有意思的机会。我觉得 AI 会彻底改变个性化体验。

turns.en: That will completely change and change the way that companies speak to consumers and how they get into consumers' wallets. Healthcare, there's something like 10,000 known diseases and only 600-ish target medicines, target drugs for those.
turns.zh: 这会完全改变企业与消费者沟通的方式、进入消费者钱包的方式。医疗方面，大约有 1 万种已知疾病，但只有 600 种左右的靶向药物。

turns.en: There will be major advances in those fields over time. So we like our bets. We like where we invest and we will express these big telescope-type things through our sectors in different ways.
turns.zh: 这些领域随着时间会有重大进展。所以我们喜欢我们的布局，喜欢我们投入的方向，我们会通过板块以不同方式体现这些大趋势。

turns.en: But we've always found the key thing is you have to be on the right side of these big structural trends, even if it means paying up and paying more and feeling uncomfortable when you pay up.
turns.zh: 但我们一直发现关键的一点是，你必须站在这些大的结构性趋势的正确一侧——即使这意味着要付出更高的价格、在出价时感到不舒服。

turns.en: Like over the long term, back to what I said around good things happen to good companies, you just tend to expose yourself to good luck when you're on the right side of these structural trends and you tend to be inundated with bad luck when you fight those things.
turns.zh: 因为从长远来看，回到我说的“好事降临到好公司”——当你站在结构性趋势的正确一侧，你自然就让自己暴露在好运之中；当你逆这些趋势而行，你就会被坏运淹没。

turns.en: That was a thoughtful way to analyze it. So you mentioned that you and Brian spend most of your time focusing on the most important investment decisions that you're going to make each year and the divestitures, the monetizations.
turns.zh: 这个分析角度很有深度。你之前提到你和 Brian 把大部分时间花在那每年最重要的投资决策和退出决策上。

turns.en: So Ken, what about the much-talked-about issue of liquidity in private equity and the exit backlog that we all talk about? How do you see it and how are you managing Premiere through that?
turns.zh: 那么，关于私募股权里被广泛讨论的流动性问题和退出积压，你怎么看？你又是怎样带着 Permira 穿越这个周期的？

turns.en: So look, the industry and the model, it only really works if there's about 20% to 25% DPI per annum. And the industry's not been delivering that.
turns.zh: 嗯，这个行业和这个模式，只有每年 DPI 达到大约 20% 到 25% 才真正行得通。而行业并没有做到这一点。

turns.en: It's not been delivering that for coming up to a handful of years now, right? I think that starts probably 10-ish percent. And that can't continue if the business model is to work and flourish.
turns.zh: 已经好几年没有做到了。我估计目前大概只有 10% 左右。如果商业模式要运转和繁荣，这不可能继续下去。

turns.en: So first of all, yes, I think it's problematic. We just take our data points in the last 12 months. Our status is 22%. And so we've realized 22% of our nav over the last 12 months.
turns.zh: 首先，是的，我觉得这是一个问题。看看我们过去 12 个月的数据——我们的分配比率是 22%。我们在过去 12 个月实现了 NAV 的 22% 的分配。

turns.en: And we've done that through a variety of different exit routes. It's not easy, but it requires you and your organization to have the mindset that DPI is an operating rhythm.
turns.zh: 我们通过多种不同的退出路径做到了这一点。这并不容易，但它要求你和你的组织有一种心态：DPI 是一种运营节奏。

turns.en: It's not an event. And frankly, and it's uncomfortable for people, but the truth is, it's ancient history the second you send the money back, right?
turns.zh: 不是一次性事件。坦率地说，这对人们来说并不舒服，但事实是，当你把钱还回去的那一刻，它就成历史了。

turns.en: And you need to be focused on the next set of things that you're going to be monetizing and bringing to market. You know, we have a centralized target setting system.
turns.zh: 你需要把注意力放在下一批准备变现和推向市场的项目上。你知道，我们有集中化的目标设定体系。

turns.en: We have an exit committee. We drive really big accountability down the organization. We set incentives that are linked to achieving those things.
turns.zh: 我们有退出委员会。我们把非常大的问责机制推到组织深处。我们设定了与达成那些目标挂钩的激励机制。

turns.en: But the single most important thing really is just having good companies. And it's cliche and it's easy to say, but good companies sell themselves and bad companies just get stuck.
turns.zh: 但真正最重要的事情就是拥有好的企业。这是老生常谈，说起来容易，但好企业自己会卖掉自己，坏企业就是会被困住。

turns.en: And the single biggest reason why we've got excess liquidity over the last 12 months and last 24 months, actually, if you go back, is actually not our processes and our incentives and our systems.
turns.zh: 过去 12 个月乃至 24 个月我们之所以有足够的流动性，如果你回溯的话，最大的原因其实并不是我们的流程、激励或系统。

turns.en: It's actually that we've got businesses that are desirable. You know, the businesses that people want to own and the reason that they want to own them is they have very long growth runways at exit.
turns.zh: 而是我们拥有令人向往的企业。人们想要拥有这些企业的原因，是它们在退出时仍然有非常长的增长跑道。

turns.en: They're not over-optimized businesses. For our viewers, can you discuss what DPI is? What does it stand for? So, you know, DPI is really just money being sent back to investors.
turns.zh: 它们不是被过度优化的企业。对于我们的观众，你能解释一下 DPI 是什么吗？它代表什么？嗯，DPI 其实就是把资金还给投资人。

turns.en: I think that's the easiest way to describe it. When we talk about percentage of NAV, that's the percentage of your unrealized net asset value.
turns.zh: 我觉得这是最简单的描述。当我们说 NAV 的百分比时，那是相对于你未实现的净资产价值而言的。

turns.en: And the way that we tend to look at it, and I think the industry tends to look at it, is how much money are you sending back as a percentage of your unrealized net asset value that you're sitting on?
turns.zh: 我们看待这个指标的方式——我想行业也是——是你以未实现净资产价值为基数，向投资人返还了多少比例的资金。

turns.en: That metric ought to be at 20 to 25 percent. Got it. Thank you for clarifying. So every investment firm talks about culture. But culture is often forged and built during periods of stress.
turns.zh: 这个指标应该在 20% 到 25% 之间。明白了，谢谢你的解释。每家投资公司都在谈文化，但文化往往是在压力时期锻造和建立的。

turns.en: Yeah. So how has Premier's culture evolved over past market cycles and how does it guide your decision-making today? So Lima Brothers and Arthur Anderson.
turns.zh: 对。Permira 的文化在过去几轮市场周期中如何演变？它今天如何指导你们的决策？嗯，Lehman Brothers 和 Arthur Andersen。

turns.en: Two different companies, two different times, two different factors, two different faces at the top of those organizations. The common theme in those organizations was, in my view, was the same thing that led to extraordinary success for each of them, led to extraordinary downfall.
turns.zh: 两家不同的公司、两个不同的时代、两个不同的因素、两批不同的掌舵人。在我来看，那两家组织的共同主题是：导致它们取得非凡成功的因素，同样也导致了她们的覆灭。

turns.en: So in the case of Arthur Anderson, they had built a really strong business, cross-selling consulting services into audit clients. And then that caught them out with Enron when they pushed that too far.
turns.zh: 比如 Arthur Andersen，他们建立了一个非常强大的业务——把咨询服务交叉销售给审计客户。然后在安然事件上翻了车，因为他们把那条路推得太远了。

turns.en: Lehman, you know, Lehman wasn't a bank. It was a broker dealer. It was borrowing short and it was investing that very aggressively on the other side.
turns.zh: Lehman——Lehman 并不是一家银行，它是一家 broker-dealer（经纪交易商）。它短借长投，另一端非常激进地投资。

turns.en: And that led to huge success over a couple of decades, until it didn't. And then the question you ask yourself is, so why was that allowed to happen?
turns.zh: 这带来了二十年的巨大成功，直到不再成功。然后你问自己的问题是：为什么这被允许发生？

turns.en: And at least in my view, they're both examples of just culture failing at scale. And I think if you walked around both of those companies, and I was a very junior person in both of those companies at the time, so I was nowhere near the top table, but there's a feeling you get being in organizations.
turns.zh: 至少在我看来，这两家都是文化在规模化时崩溃的案例。我觉得，如果你在那些公司里走过一圈——当时我非常初级，完全不在核心决策层——但在一个组织里你会有那种感觉。

turns.en: It doesn't matter what level you are. And I think the common themes in those organizations was probably you had charismatic leadership. You had really big growth ambitions.
turns.zh: 不管你是什么级别都一样。我觉得那两家公司里的共同特征大概是：你有魅力型的领导、有非常宏大的增长野心。

turns.en: You had a ton of confidence. You probably also had a culture of risk-taking that had gone too far, sort of risky practices that would like normalised.
turns.zh: 你有极大的自信。你的风险文化可能已经过了头——一些冒险的做法被常态化了。

turns.en: You had probably people that couldn't speak truth to power. You had incentives in the wrong place. And that would have been common between both of those companies.
turns.zh: 你可能有不敢对权力讲真话的人。你的激励放在了错误的地方。这两家公司都有这些共性问题。

turns.en: Yeah, those are dangerous things to have. Right. And you know, because you've built an amazing business in Goldman Sachs, there would have been a set of things that would have led to that success and continue to propel the company forward today.
turns.zh: 嗯，这些都是很危险的事情。对，你知道，Goldman Sachs 建立了一个了不起的业务，一定有一套东西促成了那个成功，并且继续推动公司向前。

turns.en: But if the culture isn't one that welcomes diversity of thought, the speaking of truth to power structures that actually risk-manage any company, including Goldman Sachs, will run into the same problem over time.
turns.zh: 但如果文化不是一个欢迎多元思考、欢迎对权力讲真话的文化——那么风险管理结构对任何公司（包括 Goldman Sachs）来说，长期都会撞上同样的问题。

turns.en: So that kind of cultural underpinning and bounded entrepreneurialism is really important. So I think that now coming back to your question around Pamira and culture, I think that you live your life forward, you understand it backwards.
turns.zh: 所以那种文化基础和有边界的创业精神非常重要。回到你关于 Permira 和文化的问题——我觉得人生要向前走，但只能在回顾中才能理解。

turns.en: And I certainly wasn't taking notes during Arthur Anderson or Lehman Brothers, but by osmosis, I think those things would have impacted the way I think about culture.
turns.zh: 我在 Arthur Andersen 和 Lehman Brothers 的时候当然没有做笔记，但通过耳儒目染，我觉得那些经历影响了我对文化的思考方式。

turns.en: Pamira is an organisation. And the number one thing I love about the organisation is it gets better out of stress. So I've always loved the book Anti-Fragility.
turns.zh: Permira 是一个组织。我最喜欢这个组织的一点是：它从压力中变得更好。我一直很喜欢《Antifragile》这本书。

turns.en: The Nasantala book is kind of a complicated book. But the core idea, I think, is quite simple. And it's that there are robust systems and they tend to endure crisis and stress.
turns.zh: Nassim Taleb 的那本读起来有点复杂，但核心观点我觉得其实很简单。就是存在鲁棒型系统，它们经历危机和压力之后能存活下来。

turns.en: And then there are anti-fragile systems that get better out of crisis and stress. And Pamira, without question, has got better and much better, much faster out of peak stress moments.
turns.zh: 然后还有反脆弱型系统，它们从危机和压力中变得更好。Permira 无疑问在经历极度压力的时刻之后，变得更好、更快。

turns.en: And I could go through a list of those moments over 40-plus years. I think the one that was most probably visible to me and I lived through and a huge part of our history was obviously the global financial crisis.
turns.zh: 在 40 多年的历史中我可以列出很多这样的时刻。我觉得对我来说最显而易见的、我亲身经历的、也是我们历史很重要篇章的——显然是全球金融危机。

turns.en: We had a fund at that time, which was, you know, full of businesses, actually pretty good businesses, but cyclical, too much cyclicality, too much leverage at the wrong time in the cycle.
turns.zh: 当时我们有一支基金，里面装的企业其实都是不错的企业，但周期性太强、在周期错误时点加了太多杠杆。

turns.en: We had invested too quickly. And when the cycle turned, you know, we, when I joined Pamira, I remember sitting in a, actually it was Tom had put up a slide and he put the fund mark up.
turns.zh: 我们投得太快了。当周期逆转的时候——我刚加入 Permira 的时候，我记得有一次开会，Tom 放了一张幻灯片，上面是基金的重估价格。

turns.en: And I thought it was a typo. And the organization, you know, we didn't lose anyone. The investors, the partners dug deep into their own pockets as we sort of had a down round in terms of the next fund cycle.
turns.zh: 我以为那是打字错误。而组织——我们没有裁掉任何人。投资人和合伙人们掏了自己的脐包——我们在下一个基金周期相当于经历了一次 down round。

turns.en: We held the keys to our businesses. We monetized at the right time. We did some great investing in the rest of that fund, actually things like Renaissance Learning and Ancestry were part of the part of that fund, too.
turns.zh: 我们守住了企业的控制权。我们在正确的时间变现了。在那支基金的剩余部分我们做了一些很好的投资——Renaissance Learning 和 Ancestry 也在那支基金里。

turns.en: That fund ended up emerging as a top quarter fund. Wow, that's so good. And we got better out of that. We also pivoted our strategy at that time to much higher quality businesses, resilience, growth, structural growth.
turns.zh: 那支基金最终成了一支前四分之一的基金。哇，太棒了。我们从那里面变得更优秀了。我们当时也转型了策略，转向更高质量的企业——韧性、增长、结构性增长。

turns.en: And that's the core of our strategy today that we prosecute through our sectors. And so, yeah, I mean, culture for me, and that's the thing that I'm most focused on, probably those two things.
turns.zh: 那就是我们今天核心策略的基础，通过我们的板块去执行。所以对于我来讴，文化——这是我关注最多的事情——大概就是这两点。

turns.en: One is not running into that Lehman Arthur Anderson problem. Having the confidence to know what you do and do well and drive deeper and deeper into that and always reevaluating first principles, whether what you're in and doing is the right thing on the one hand and then making sure we've got an organization that is able to not just endure but come out of stressful situations in a better place.
turns.zh: 第一，不要变成 Lehman 或 Arthur Andersen 那样。要有信心知道自己做什么、做得好，然后越扎越深，同时始终从第一性原理出发重新审视自己在做的事情是否正确。第二，确保我们有一个组织，不仅能承受压力，而且能在压力之后以更好的姿态走出来。

turns.en: Yeah, so it's the confidence with humility. Exactly. So that culture also expresses itself beyond your portfolio. And Premier has made a significant commitment to philanthropy through its foundation.
turns.zh: 对，这就是自信与谦逊的并存。正是如此。那么这种文化也延伸到了你们投资组合之外。Permira 通过其基金会做出了重大的公益承诺。

turns.en: How did that initiative begin? And what makes it important to the firm today? We set out the Premier Foundation 10 years ago. We backed today about 35 organizations.
turns.zh: 这个倡议是怎么开始的？为什么它对公司今天如此重要？我们在 10 年前设立了 Permira 基金会。目前支持大约 35 个组织。

turns.en: 80% of the professionals in our organization have donated like significant time. And I donated significant time to Pro Bono, to these organizations.
turns.zh: 我们组织中 80% 的专业人士都投入了大量时间做 Pro Bono（公益服务），为这些组织出力。

turns.en: So it's really important culturally for us. We just took the decision this year to make the foundation a permanent carryholder in our funds.
turns.zh: 所以这对我们的文化非常重要。今年我们做了一个决定，让基金会成为我们基金的永久性 carried interest（附带权益）持有人。

turns.en: That's interesting. So we think we're one of the very few firms, maybe the only firm that at least I know of that has done that and that's quite a big ask to go to our partners and say, permanently we want this foundation to be aligned with the outcomes that we drive.
turns.zh: 这很有意思。我们可能是极少数这样做的公司——至少据我所知是唯一的——而这需要跟合伙人提一个很大的要求：我们希望这个基金会永久性地与我们驱动的成果绑定在一起。

turns.en: So yeah, it's an important thing. We thank you for asking about it because we never really get to talk about it. But it is important inside our organization.
turns.zh: 所以，是的，这是一件重要的事情。感谢你问到这个，因为我们平时很少有机会谈论它。但在我们组织内部它很重要。

turns.en: We do talk about it and most often we only talk about it inside our business. Yeah, well, it's showing a lot of leadership in the industry. I have not heard of anyone putting carry in their foundation.
turns.zh: 我们确实会讨论这个话题，只不过通常只在内部说。嗯，这确实是在行业中展现了领导力。我还没听说过哪家公司把 carried interest 放进自己的基金会。

turns.en: That's fantastic. So you and Brian are part of a new generation of private equity leaders. And looking across the industry more broadly, where do you think your generation of leaders will take private equity over the next decade?
turns.zh: 这太了不起了。你和 Brian 是新一代私募股权领导者的一部分。把目光放远到整个行业，你觉得你们这一代领导者会把私募股权带向何方？

turns.en: It's a great question. I mean, look, the industry is bifurcating, right? That's no secret. And you have two very distinct business models emerging and you have people that are generally private, generally very narrow and deep in what they do.
turns.zh: 好问题。行业正在分化，这没什么秘密。有两种截然不同的商业模式正在浮现——有些公司是私人持有的、非常专注和深入。

turns.en: And they live or die on whether they perform or not. And there are pluses and minuses that model. And then there are firms that are building their businesses through newer and newer business lines, scaling their products.
turns.zh: 他们的生存取决于业绩表现。这种模式有优点也有缺点。然后还有一些公司在通过不断推出新业务线、扩展产品来建设业务。

turns.en: And breadth is really important to those firms. The retail channels really important to those firms, but it's like a different set of considerations.
turns.zh: 广度对那些公司非常重要。零售渠道对它们非常重要，但那是另一套考量。

turns.en: I can't speak to both. I can only really speak to what we're doing and probably what the set of people, new leadership in this part of the world are thinking about.
turns.zh: 我没法两边都评论。我只能说我们在做什么，以及可能这部分世界新一代领导者在思考什么。

turns.en: I'm just really excited about a really simple thing, which is building an organization with a really distinct investing culture. It becomes the talent magnet for people that want to be craftspeople and just generating superior outcomes over the long term and doing that consistently.
turns.zh: 我真正兴奋的是一件很简单的事情：打造一个有着鲜明投资文化的组织，让它成为匠人的磁场，持续创造卓越的长期回报。

turns.en: And that is no mean feat. That's really hard to do. It requires just a persistent level of dissatisfaction with every single part of your business and just constantly turning stones up and asking why we can't be better and pushing and investing and thinking long term, being willing to skate to where the puck is going, not where it is today.
turns.zh: 这绝非易事，真的很难做到。它需要你对业务的每一个部分都保持一种持续的不满足感，不断翻开石头问我们为什么不能更好——不断推动、投入、长远思考，愿意滑向冰球将要去的方向而不是现在的位置。

turns.en: Those things are easy to say. They're really hard to do and force yourself to do every day. But I've been with the firm 17 years. I'd love to be with the firm another 17 years.
turns.zh: 这些事情说起来容易，做起来真的很难——每天逼自己做到。但我在公司已经 17 年了，我希望再待 17 年。

turns.en: And Brian, I know feels the same way. And I think that's what we're most excited about doing. That's great. So on a personal level, you grew up in an immigrant family and watched your father scale a business from the ground up.
turns.zh: 我知道 Brian 也是这么想的。我觉得这就是我们最兴奋要去做的事情。太棒了。聊点个人的——你在一个移民家庭长大，看着父亲从零开始把生意做大。

turns.en: How did that firsthand look at entrepreneurship shape your worldview and your approach to backing founders today? My dad became into the country in his probably mid-20s.
turns.zh: 那种对创业的亲身体验如何塑造了你的世界观，以及你今天支持创始人的方式？我父亲大概 25 岁左右到了这个国家。

turns.en: Had a single store, long story short. Scaled that to about 60 stores in really like prime locations across London. These are grocery stores.
turns.zh: 一开始只有一家店，长话短说，他把规模做到了大约 60 家店——都是伦敦非常好的位置。这些是杂货店。

turns.en: Did a very small P2P, a public to private, in the middle of that. Sold that business to Tesco in 2000. He found another business, scaled that over about 20 years.
turns.zh: 中间做了一个很小的 P2P（公有公司私有化），然后在 2000 年把那个业务卖给了 Tesco。他又发现了一个新业务，花了大约 20 年把它做大。

turns.en: Sold that to Apex France, a roll up they were doing there. And you know, he's 75 now and he's looking for the next thing to do. I think I was relatively kind of street smart probably from an early age, just from seeing that kind of stuff ground up.
turns.zh: 卖给了 Apex France，他们在法国做的一个 roll-up（并购整合）。他现在 75 岁了，还在找下一件事做。我觉得我从小因为看到这些东西，相对比较有“街头智慧”。

turns.en: I also just developed an empathy for founders. I am not a founder. And actually, my dad always tells me that. You won't ever understand what that really means to go to bed at night and have on your shoulders an organization in that way.
turns.zh: 我也因此对创始人有一种同理心。我不是创始人。实际上我父亲总是跟我说：你永远无法真正理解——晚上睡觉时肩上抗着一个组织是什么感觉。

turns.en: I think that's just a completely different thing. But the grit, just the sheer work ethic of just watching that was huge. The sort of the risk taking and the calibration of that risk taking and the confidence and paranoia that that takes, you know, it's stuck with me.
turns.zh: 我觉得那完全是另一回事。但从旁观察那种 grit（韧性）、纯粹的工作强度、那种冒险和风险的精确校准、那种自信与偏执的并存——这些一直留在我身上。

turns.en: Makes total sense. Really an impressive entrepreneurial background. Yeah. It's fabulous. So I'd like to end these conversations with a lightning round.
turns.zh: 完全理解。真是一段厉害的创业家庭履历。嗯。太精彩了。我想用一个 lightning round（快问快答）来结束这次对话。

turns.en: Yep. Just ask you some short answer questions. So what do you think your personal greatest strength is as an investor? I'd say knowing what I don't know and knowing where to get it.
turns.zh: 嗯。就问你一些简短的问题。你觉得你作为投资者最大的优势是什么？我觉得是知道自己不知道什么，以及知道去哪里找到答案。

turns.en: Okay. What was the very first investment you ever made? That was actually before Renaissance learning and another project I started with was a company called Sagem.
turns.zh: 好。你做过的第一笔投资是什么？那其实是在 Renaissance Learning 之前，我起步的另一个项目是一家叫 Sagem 的公司。

turns.en: It was a carve-out from Siemens. What's the best piece of advice you've ever received? I think in the investing sphere probably, I always think about the, I think it was Howard Mark's phrase, the four most dangerous words in investing are this time is different.
turns.zh: 那是从 Siemens 分拆出来的。你收到过的最好的建议是什么？我觉得在投资领域大概是——我总是想起一句话，我记得是 Howard Marks 说的，投资中最危险的四个字是“这次不一样”。

turns.en: We talked about that earlier in your investment committee. How do you spend your time out of the office? I've got three kids, nine, 11, 13. And you know, I mean, this job is, it's seven days a week and it's very intense.
turns.zh: 你们之前在投委会讨论过这个。不工作的时候你怎么安排时间？我有三个孩子，9 岁、11 岁、13 岁。这个工作是每周七天的，强度非常大。

turns.en: And so virtually all my time, I try and spend with my wife and my kids. And that's the first priority. If I'm not doing that, I love sport, I love life sport.
turns.zh: 所以几乎所有的业余时间我都尽量花在老婆和孩子身上。那是第一优先级。如果不是陪家人，我喜欢体育，我爱看球。

turns.en: I'm a season ticket holder at Liverpool. I travel the length and breadth of the country and countries to follow the team. And that's the most likely place you'll find me is Anfield, if I'm not with my family.
turns.zh: 我是利物浦的季票持有者。我到处跟随球队，英国和国外都去。如果我不在家里，最可能找到我的地方就是 Anfield。

turns.en: Which investor do you admire most? I think Chris Hone probably for the way he thinks, Buffett for his temperament, probably Munger in the same, same breath and Howard Marks for sort of like risk management.
turns.zh: 你最敬佩哪位投资者？我觉得 Chris Hohn 大概是他的思考方式，Buffett 是他的心态，Munger 也是同等位置，Howard Marks 是他的风险管理。

turns.en: So yeah, the, the, the standard grades, so to say. Well, very impressive. Investors. And finally, what are you most excited about in the world right now?
turns.zh: 所以呃，都是一些经典的选择吧。非常了不起的投资者。最后一个问题，你现在对世界上什么最感到兴奋？

turns.en: The whole thing. Everything we talked about, it's a great time to be alive. It's a great time to be alive. Yeah. Anyway, Dupont, thank you so much for joining me.
turns.zh: 所有的一切。我们聊到的所有东西，这是一个活着的好时代。这确实是一个好时代。嗯。不过了，Dipan，非常感谢你来到节目。

turns.en: Thank you. This was a great conversation. Thank you. Really enjoyed it. Thank you all for listening to this episode of Goldman Sachs Exchange's Great Investors, which was recorded on July 28th, 2026.
turns.zh: 谢谢。这是一场很槍的对话。谢谢。真的很享受。感谢大家收听这一期 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 的 Great Investors，本期录制于 2026 年 7 月 28 日。
